facts.text: A proving ground is a closed, controlled area where the complete real machine and its real sensors are tested against physical targets; a track test is one such test, and a whole-machine test is any test in which nothing is simulated.
facts.quote: A proving ground is a closed, controlled area where the complete real machine, with its real sensors, is tested against physical targets; a track test is one such test, and a whole-machine test is any test in which nothing is simulated.

facts.text: Whole-machine testing uses a real loader, a real operator or robot driver, and a real test body positioned where a worker would be; measuring equipment records when the machine warned, when it braked, and where it stopped.
facts.quote: a real loader, a real operator or a robot driver, a real test body standing where a worker would be, and measuring equipment that records exactly when the machine warned, when it braked and where it stopped.
